raw_response:
I keep it steady this year. I am old now, only two people in the house, so I cannot spread myself too thin. Wheat and maize are still my main stomach and cash crops, same as before. I leave most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is what I know best and it keeps grain in hand. I keep a smaller piece for stevia because if the buyer comes and the price is alright, that gives extra cash, but I do not want too much of it because it needs more watching and hand work. I will not gamble on fancy seed or very heavy fertilizer. If I spend too much early and then the crop has trouble, that money is gone. So I use what worked before, a little on the safe side for grain, and I save some cash for water and medicine if I really need it.

For the wheat already in the field, I will watch the stand and give water from the well around jointing and again around grain filling if the sky stays dry. If the leaves look pale, I will topdress some urea, but not too much because fertilizer costs money. After wheat harvest I move fast on maize, no delay, because if I plant late the autumn cold can hurt yield. On the stevia land, I will prepare the ground clean, plant in late April, give some base fertilizer, and irrigate a few times because that crop does not like to sit dry after transplanting. I use family labor as much as I can and only hire a few days when work bunches up at harvest or hand weeding.
